title: Convert RAW to JPEG on iPhone: Keep the Editable Original
description: Convert a device-compatible RAW photo to a separate JPEG copy when the recipient needs a widely supported image.
direct: Make a JPEG from a RAW photo when the recipient needs an easy-to-open copy. Save it separately so you can still adjust the original exposure and color later.
figureAlt: A RAW original stays archived while a separate JPEG picture is shared.

cards.choice.heading: Check compatibility first
cards.choice.body: RAW is a family of camera formats. A phone supporting one camera’s files does not establish support for every RAW file. Try a representative original before starting a large batch.
sections.explain.heading: A conversion is a rendering decision
sections.explain.body: Apple explains that ProRAW provides flexibility for exposure, color and white-balance editing. Once rendered to JPEG, those decisions are represented in pixels with less editing latitude. The JPEG may look different from another RAW preview because rendering differs; that alone is not evidence of damage or improvement.
sections.practice.heading: Know the limits before batching
sections.practice.body: Our app lists device-compatible RAW inputs up to 60 megapixels and batch conversion. It does not promise every camera decoder or identical rendering to a desktop editor. The first three successful photo conversions are free, and each image in a batch counts; further conversions require purchase. Keep originals, especially if you expect to revisit exposure or color.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: What if my phone cannot open a particular RAW file?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: Try a compatible editor that supports that camera model. Keep the untouched file and export a JPEG there before trying the rest of the batch.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: Why does the JPEG differ from the preview I saw in another editor?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: RAW editors can choose different defaults for exposure, white balance and color. Compare the actual JPEG in the intended viewer before assuming the conversion failed.

steps.step-1.text: Select a compatible RAW original in PhotoFix: HDR to Normal Photos on iPhone.
steps.step-2.text: Choose RAW-to-JPEG conversion and decide whether to retain capture date and location. Review the rendered photo.
steps.step-3.text: Export the JPEG copy and open it in the receiving app. Keep the RAW file and check actual dimensions and appearance.
